chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who is afflicted with a nosebleed while he is in salat (prayer). He said: If he is able to reach water near him, to his right, or to his left, or in front of him, while he is still facing the qiblah, then he should wash it off and then complete what remains of his salat (prayer). But if he is not able to reach water before turning his face away or speaking, then his salat (prayer) has been invalidated.

key_terms.قَطَعَ صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer) has been interrupted or invalidated
key_terms.مُسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةِ: remaining oriented toward the qiblah during salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَنْصَرِفَ بِوَجْهِهِ: to turn his face away from the qiblah

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he gets a nosebleed during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning nosebleeding during salat (prayer). If a person can wash away the blood without breaking the posture and orientation of salat (prayer), he completes it; otherwise, if he turns away or speaks before doing so, the salat (prayer) is cut off.
